title: Lead Scoring Model Overview
text: The B2B Lead Scoring Model evaluates 2,375 employers and 125 brokers. It uses a composite score calculated as 0.4 * fit_score + 0.6 * account_engagement + 0.8 * broker_bonus. The model outputs a Tier (Priority MQL, MQL, Responder, Disqualified) and an Archetype (Champion, Achiever, Watcher, Dormant Giant, Fader, Lurker, Detractor). This is a deterministic, heuristic prioritization framework, not a predictive conversion model.

title: Fit Score Calculation Rules
text: Fit score is based on: Renewal proximity (25 points if <=30 days, 20 if <=60 days, 15 if <=90 days, 5 if <=180 days); Premium size (25 points if >=$2M, 20 if >=$1M, 15 if >=$500K, 10 if >=$100K); Industry fit (15 points for target industries such as Healthcare, Technology, Finance, Manufacturing, and Professional Services; 8 for Adjacent; 0 for Non-Target); Carrier presence (10 points for Aetna, UnitedHealth, or Cigna); and Broker presence (15 points).

title: Engagement Score Rules
text: Engagement is calculated from email and webinar activities. Email points range from 2 (generic) to 20 (high_intent), with half-life decay. Webinar points include attendance (5), minutes (up to 5), polls (2), questions (5), and downloads (5). Account engagement = best contact score + 0.3 * the scores of other contacts + a 10-point multi-stakeholder bonus if at least 2 contacts are engaged.

title: Tiering Definitions
text: Tier assignment follows the deterministic Python function determine_tier(score, premium, engagement): Priority MQL if premium >= $1,000,000 AND engagement >=15 AND total score >=70. Active signals such as urgent renewal, multi-threaded engagement, or broker engagement may be used as sales context, but they are not hard gates in the current tier function. MQL if total score >=50 and the Priority MQL conditions are not met. Responder if total score <50 and engagement >0. Disqualified if total score <50 and engagement is 0. The current determine_tier function does not independently check competitor domains; any competitor exclusion must be implemented and documented separately if required.

title: Archetype Definitions
text: Champion: high fit (>=60), high engagement (>=40), and multi-threaded. Achiever: high fit and high engagement, but single-threaded. Watcher: high fit, moderate engagement (15-40), and no high-intent signals. Dormant Giant: high fit and low engagement (<15). Fader: low fit and moderate engagement (5-15). Lurker: low fit and low engagement. Detractor: Disqualified. These are descriptive segment definitions; the package currently does not provide a separately verified executable archetype-assignment function. Where definitions overlap at boundary values, apply a documented precedence rule before assigning one exclusive archetype.

title: Limitations & Caveats
text: This is a synthetic dataset. The scoring weights (0.4, 0.6, 0.8) are heuristic and are not derived from actual closed-won revenue. A high total score indicates prioritization, not a guaranteed conversion or calibrated probability. Archetypes and scoring rules should be validated against real sales cycles before operational use.

title: Tier Scorecard Summary
text: Reference tier counts: Disqualified = 475 accounts (0 SQLs), MQL = 1,134 accounts (498 SQLs), Priority MQL = 185 accounts (117 SQLs), Responder = 581 accounts (0 SQLs). These tier counts sum to 2,375 employers.

title: Archetype Scorecard Summary
text: Reference archetype counts currently recorded: Champions = 145, Achievers = 210, Watchers = 350, Dormant Giants = 420, Faders = 500, Lurkers = 750, Detractors = 475. These counts sum to 2,850, which is 475 higher than the stated 2,375-employer population. Treat this scorecard as unreconciled; do not present it as a mutually exclusive distribution of the same 2,375 employers until the underlying population, duplicates, or aggregation method is checked.
